evals.prompt: I'm a 32-year-old desk worker, 78kg, 178cm. I want to gain muscle but only have 3 evenings a week for the gym. Build me a 12-week plan.
evals.description: Standard hypertrophy plan with constrained schedule.
expected_output_criteria: Recommends a 3-day split (e.g., upper/lower/full or push/pull/legs) appropriate for the schedule
Specifies sets, reps, and rest intervals per exercise rather than just listing movements
Provides a calorie surplus target with a concrete daily kcal range and protein in grams/day
Phases the 12 weeks (e.g., volume → intensity → deload) with clear progression rules
Names recovery, sleep, and tracking metrics the user should monitor weekly

evals.prompt: I have lower back pain when I deadlift and my doctor cleared me for general training but said 'avoid heavy spinal loading'. I still want to get stronger. What do I do?
evals.description: Medium case with a medical constraint that must shape the plan.
expected_output_criteria: Acknowledges the medical constraint as a hard limit, not a suggestion
Substitutes deadlift with named lower-spine-friendly alternatives (e.g., trap bar deadlift, hip thrust, kettlebell swing) with rationale
Recommends a structured warm-up and mobility routine targeting the lower back specifically
Defines a clear stop/scale-back rule (e.g., 'if pain >3/10, deload')
Avoids prescribing rehab exercises; defers to physio for diagnosis-level work

evals.prompt: I'm cutting and stalled at 76kg for 5 weeks. I'm eating 1800 kcal, training 5x/week, getting 7 hours sleep, and tracking everything. Help.
evals.description: Hard case requiring root-cause analysis of a fat-loss plateau.
expected_output_criteria: Asks for or estimates maintenance kcal to determine if the deficit is real
Lists at least 3 common causes of a plateau (under-reporting intake, NEAT decline, water retention, metabolic adaptation) and how to test each
Proposes a specific next intervention (diet break, refeed, recalculation) with a 1-2 week test window
Warns against arbitrarily cutting kcal further as a first move
Defines what 'fixed' looks like (e.g., 0.5% bodyweight drop/week sustained for 2 weeks) so progress is measurable
